title: Heracles: The Nemean Lion
subtitle: An unbreakable hide, bare hands, and the skin he wears forever

main.excerpt: When Hercules heard that, he went to Tiryns and did as he was bid by Eurystheus. First, Eurystheus ordered him to bring the skin of the Nemean lion; now that was an invulnerable beast begotten by Typhon. On his way to attack the lion he came to Cleonae and lodged at the house of a day-laborer, Molorchus;

combat.excerpt: And having come to Nemea and tracked the lion, he first shot an arrow at him, but when he perceived that the beast was invulnerable, he heaved up his club and made after him. And when the lion took refuge in a cave with two mouths, Hercules built up the one entrance and came in upon the beast through the other, and putting his arm round its neck held it tight till he had choked it

narrativeBlocks.title: The first labour
narrativeBlocks.body: The Nemean lion is no ordinary beast — offspring of monsters, hide proof against every weapon. It has been terrorising Nemea; no arrow or blade can touch it.

narrativeBlocks.title: When weapons fail
narrativeBlocks.body: Heracles looses arrows at the beast — they bounce off its hide like rain. He chases it into its cave, blocks the exits, and does the only thing left: strangles it barehanded.

narrativeBlocks.title: The trophy that dresses him
narrativeBlocks.body: He can't skin the invulnerable hide with a knife — so he uses the lion's own claws, the only things sharp enough to cut it. The pelt becomes his signature: the lionskin and club you see in every image of Heracles start here.

narrativeBlocks.title: Eurystheus's terror
narrativeBlocks.body: When Heracles returns wearing the beast that was supposed to kill him, Eurystheus forbids him from entering the city again — the labours must be reported at the gates. The king is so afraid he keeps a bronze jar buried as a hiding place.

narrativeBlocks.title: The signature image
narrativeBlocks.body: Everything in the iconic Heracles — the club, the lionskin, the wrestling — comes from this single story. It is the pattern for every strength-labour after it: when the tool fails, the body doesn't.

quiz.prompt: How does Heracles kill the Nemean lion?

choices.text: He shoots it with poisoned arrows
He traps it in a bronze jar
He strangles it barehanded — its hide is proof against every weapon
He blinds it and it starves

quiz.explanation: Arrows bounce off the monster's hide; Heracles corners it in its cave and chokes it to death.

quiz.prompt: Why does Heracles wear the lion's skin?

choices.text: As armour against the remaining labours
As a disguise to enter Nemea
As the trophy of his first labour — he skins it with the beast's own claws and it becomes his signature garb

quiz.explanation: The lionskin (with club) becomes the universal identifier of Heracles in art and story.
